Manual/scripted claude plugin marketplace update reuses your existing git credential helpers, so HTTPS via gh auth login/Keychain/git-credential-store, or SSH via a key loaded in ssh-agent, works the same as a normal git pull in your terminal.
Answer/Official from Create and distribute a plugin marketplace - Claude Code Docs
Private-repository credential caveat that a naive cron job can also hit:

Background auto-update is more fragile: by default it disables git credential helpers for its git pull, so private HTTPS remotes can't authenticate even with a helper configured; SSH remotes with ssh-agent are unaffected. A failed background pull falls back to a full re-clone (which does use stored credentials but can time out on large repos), so private-marketplace auto-updates "may fail intermittently."
Answer/Official from Create and distribute a plugin marketplace - Claude Code Docs
Private-repository credential caveat that a naive cron job can also hit:

To make a scheduled/background update reliable for a private HTTPS marketplace: configure a git URL rewrite scoped to that marketplace's repo or org with an embedded token (so the pull authenticates directly and skips the re-clone path), and/or set CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE=1 so a failed pull keeps the last-synced clone instead of deleting it. In CI/cron contexts, gh auth setup-git (or an equivalent credential helper) makes the fallback re-clone work unattended too.

Answer/Official from Manage sessions and Desktop application:
If I rename a Claude/Code CLI session with /rename, can I resume it in Claude/Desktop/Code?

Short answer: No. /rename creates a resume handle that only the CLI honors, and the Code tab keeps a session history of its own — a CLI session never appears in its sidebar, named or not. The one bridge runs the other way: /desktop hands the live CLI session over to the app.
If I rename a Claude/Code CLI session with /rename, can I resume it in Claude/Desktop/Code?

What /rename buys you, and where: the name shows on the prompt bar and in the /resume picker, and becomes a resume handle — claude --resume <name> or /resume <name>, resolved across the current repository and its worktrees. It replaces the AI-generated session title, which is display-only and is not a resume handle.
If I rename a Claude/Code CLI session with /rename, can I resume it in Claude/Desktop/Code?

Why the Code tab can't see it: the docs state plainly that the desktop app, Claude Code on the web, and the VS Code extension "each maintain their own session history." The CLI–Desktop relationship is spelled out under Coming from the CLI?: both can run at once on the same machine and even the same project, and "Each maintains separate session history, but they share configuration and project memory via CLAUDE.md files." Config and memory are shared; the session list is not.
If I rename a Claude/Code CLI session with /rename, can I resume it in Claude/Desktop/Code?

There is no /resume in the Code tab to begin with. The CLI-flag equivalence table maps --resume / --continue to "Click a session in the sidebar" — and that sidebar is a list of Desktop's own sessions, filterable by status, project, and environment, with no picker or search that reaches into CLI history.

Rename direction that does cross over: renaming a Remote Control session from claude.ai or the Claude app applies the same name in the CLI (needs Claude Code v2.1.221+). The actual bridge — /desktop: run it in the terminal and Claude saves the session, opens it in the desktop app, and exits the CLI. Constraints: macOS and x64 Windows, signed in with a Claude subscription; unavailable with API-key auth or on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry. It is a one-way handoff of the session you are sitting in — not a picker for arbitrary past CLI sessions.

A structural reason beyond the store split: every Code tab session in a git repository gets its own isolated worktree under <project-root>/.claude/worktrees/ (see git/worktree), plus the status, PR, and environment metadata the sidebar filters, groups, and auto-archives on.
